problem: AI agents stream tokens, call tools, share state and pause for humans, and every framework wires this to the user interface differently. AG-UI gives developers one standard way to connect any agent to any app.

stack.frontend: TypeScript client SDK (@ag-ui/client); CopilotKit on Next.js in scaffolded apps, a terminal client, and a 'dojo' demo app
stack.backend: Python (FastAPI example, ag-ui-protocol package), TypeScript and .NET SDKs, with many agent-framework integrations
stack.ai: Framework-agnostic: integrations for LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra, Pydantic AI, LlamaIndex, Agno, AG2, OpenAI Agents, Claude Agent SDK, Vercel AI SDK, Google ADK, AWS Strands, Microsoft Agent Framework and more; generated templates call OpenAI
stack.deploy: npm and Python packages, a create-ag-ui-app CLI, docs site; monorepo built with pnpm and Nx

whatsNew: It defines one open, event-based protocol: the agent streams typed events (text, tool calls, state updates, human pauses) over HTTP, and any client can render them. The 1.0 spec is frozen with a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python and .NET SDKs are generated from it.
